--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.add_visibility_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Add the natural visibility graph of a time series. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.add_visibility_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Add the natural visibility graph of a time series. title: >- [Graph.add_visibility_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Add the natural visibility graph of a time series. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add the natural visibility graph of a time series. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L14786-L14883){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.add_visibility_graph( series, value_attr="value", type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Visibility graph](../assets/graphs/add-visibility-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three natural visibility graphs of short time series, each value drawn as a dashed stem rising from a baseline with its node on top. Two values are joined when the straight line between their tops clears every value in between, so neighbors in time are always joined and a tall value such as the 5 in the last series sees far in both directions." width="100%"} Creates one node per value of `series`, in order, and joins two time points when they can "see" each other: drawing the series as bars, two bar tops are joined if the straight line between them passes strictly above every bar in between. Neighboring points always see each other, so the graph contains the path through the series, and peaks see far, so they become hubs. The construction (Lacasa et al. 2008) turns a time series into a network whose structure reflects the series: periodic series give regular graphs, random ones exponential degree distributions, and fractal ones power laws. It is NetworkX's `visibility_graph()`. A point exactly on the line blocks the view, as in NetworkX. Slopes are compared by cross-multiplication, which is exact for integer values; NetworkX computes the line and can round the other way when integer points are exactly collinear. Each node's value is stored in the `value_attr=` node attribute. In a directed graph every edge points forward in time. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Visibility graphs are useful for: - analyzing time series with network measures (degree distribution, clustering, motifs), e.g. to tell chaotic from random signals - detecting peaks and regime changes, since high points get high degree - comparing series through the networks they generate ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [series]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The time series, as a list of finite numbers. [value_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["value"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute that stores each node's value. Default is `"value"`. Pass `None` to skip storing it. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a value is not a finite number. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The peak at the third position sees everything up to the `3`, which hides the last point from it, while the low points only see their two neighbors: ::: {#101748ad .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_visibility_graph([2, 1, 5, 1, 3, 1]) graph.get_edges_str_repr() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['1--2', '1--3', '2--3', '3--4', '3--5', '4--5', '5--6'] ``` ::: ::: Each node keeps its value, and the peak has the highest degree: ::: {#525d58b7 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_node_df().select("label", "value", "degree") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
